scene.label: Act 3, Scene 5
scene.title: Scene V. Another Room in Leonato's House.

content.text: Enter Leonato and Dogberry and Verges.

lines.text: What would you with me, honest neighbour?
lines.plainText: What would you with me honest neighbour

lines.text: Marry, sir, I would have some confidence with you, that decerns you nearly.
lines.plainText: Marry sir I would have some confidence with you that decerns you nearly

lines.text: Brief, I pray you; for you see it is a busy time with me.
lines.plainText: Brief I pray you for you see it is a busy time with me

lines.text: Marry, this it is, sir.
lines.plainText: Marry this it is sir

lines.text: Yes, in truth it is, sir.
lines.plainText: Yes in truth it is sir

lines.text: What is it, my good friends?
lines.plainText: What is it my good friends

lines.text: Goodman Verges, sir, speaks a little off the matter: an old man, sir, and his wits are not so blunt as, God help, I would desire they were; but, in faith, honest as the skin between his brows.
lines.plainText: Goodman Verges sir speaks a little off the matter an old man sir and his wits are not so blunt as God help I would desire they were but in faith honest as the skin between his brows

lines.text: Yes, I thank God, I am as honest as any man living, that is an old man and no honester than I.
lines.plainText: Yes I thank God I am as honest as any man living that is an old man and no honester than I

lines.text: Comparisons are odorous: palabras, neighbour Verges.
lines.plainText: Comparisons are odorous palabras neighbour Verges

lines.text: Neighbours, you are tedious.
lines.plainText: Neighbours you are tedious

lines.text: It pleases your worship to say so, but we are the poor Duke's officers; but truly, for mine own part, if I were as tedious as a king, I could find in my heart to bestow it all of your worship.
lines.plainText: It pleases your worship to say so but we are the poor Duke's officers but truly for mine own part if I were as tedious as a king I could find in my heart to bestow it all of your worship

lines.text: All thy tediousness on me! ah?
lines.plainText: All thy tediousness on me ah

lines.text: Yea, and 'twere a thousand pound more than 'tis; for I hear as good exclamation on your worship, as of any man in the city, and though I be but a poor man, I am glad to hear it.
lines.plainText: Yea and 'twere a thousand pound more than 'tis for I hear as good exclamation on your worship as of any man in the city and though I be but a poor man I am glad to hear it

lines.text: And so am I.
lines.plainText: And so am I

lines.text: I would fain know what you have to say.
lines.plainText: I would fain know what you have to say

lines.text: Marry, sir, our watch tonight, excepting your worship's presence, ha' ta'en a couple of as arrant knaves as any in Messina.
lines.plainText: Marry sir our watch tonight excepting your worship's presence ha' ta'en a couple of as arrant knaves as any in Messina

lines.text: A good old man, sir; he will be talking; as they say, 'when the age is in, the wit is out.' God help us! it is a world to see! Well said, i' faith, neighbour Verges: well, God's a good man; and two men ride of a horse, one must ride behind. An honest soul, i' faith, sir; by my troth he is, as ever broke bread; but God is to be worshipped: all men are not alike; alas! good neighbour.
lines.plainText: A good old man sir he will be talking as they say 'when the age is in the wit is out' God help us it is a world to see Well said i' faith neighbour Verges well God's a good man and two men ride of a horse one must ride behind An honest soul i' faith sir by my troth he is as ever broke bread but God is to be worshipped all men are not alike alas good neighbour

lines.text: Indeed, neighbour, he comes too short of you.
lines.plainText: Indeed neighbour he comes too short of you

lines.text: Gifts that God gives.
lines.plainText: Gifts that God gives

lines.text: I must leave you.
lines.plainText: I must leave you

lines.text: One word, sir: our watch, sir, have indeed comprehended two aspicious persons, and we would have them this morning examined before your worship.
lines.plainText: One word sir our watch sir have indeed comprehended two aspicious persons and we would have them this morning examined before your worship

lines.text: Take their examination yourself, and bring it me: I am now in great haste, as may appear unto you.
lines.plainText: Take their examination yourself and bring it me I am now in great haste as may appear unto you

lines.text: It shall be suffigance.
lines.plainText: It shall be suffigance

lines.text: Drink some wine ere you go: fare you well.
lines.plainText: Drink some wine ere you go fare you well

lines.text: My lord, they stay for you to give your daughter to her husband.
lines.plainText: My lord they stay for you to give your daughter to her husband

lines.text: I'll wait upon them: I am ready.
lines.plainText: I'll wait upon them I am ready

lines.text: Go, good partner, go get you to Francis Seacoal; bid him bring his pen and inkhorn to the gaol: we are now to examination these men.
lines.plainText: Go good partner go get you to Francis Seacoal bid him bring his pen and inkhorn to the gaol we are now to examination these men

lines.text: And we must do it wisely.
lines.plainText: And we must do it wisely

lines.text: We will spare for no wit, I warrant you; here's that shall drive some of them to a non-come: only get the learned writer to set down our excommunication, and meet me at the gaol.
lines.plainText: We will spare for no wit I warrant you here's that shall drive some of them to a noncome only get the learned writer to set down our excommunication and meet me at the gaol
